summary.en: Artists such as Aretha Franklin push southern soul forward and outward—even when the records are not wholly made in the South.
summary.zh: Aretha Franklin等艺人推动了南部灵魂乐的发展、传播，哪怕这类风格的唱片并不完全产自“南部”。

body.zh:
Aretha Franklin等艺人推动了南部灵魂乐的发展、传播，哪怕这类风格的唱片并不完全产自“南部”。
对于Stax的唱片，或者更宽泛地说，对于由Stax和Atlantic共同主导的南部灵魂乐，有一整个稳定的艺人阵容推动了它的发展。如我上一节课所讲，不同于圆滑、专业的Motown之声，这些Stax的艺人在大众眼里更显真诚，他们的声音也更为粗犷，同时更自由、更奔放。那么，现在我们就来了解其中几位。
先从Otis Redding开始吧。说到Stax旗下的艺人，既然Stax和Atlantic联系密切，我们就有必要分清哪些人真正跟Stax签了约，而哪些又其实隶属于Atlantic。Otis Redding是真正跟Stax签约的艺人。他在60年代早期就有歌曲成为热门，到1965年，又凭着《Mr. Pitiful》这样的歌曲实现了跨界；这首歌在R&B榜单位列第10名，而在流行榜单上排名第41位。还有《Respect》，这首歌最初是由Otis Redding创作、演唱的，后来则成了Aretha Franklin的标志性歌曲——稍后我们会谈到这个。《Respect》是他在1965年推出的热门歌曲，这首歌在R&B榜单上位列第4名，但只登上了流行榜单的第35名。说到这里，大家可以回忆一下我讲过的，Motown出品音乐的排名情况。而现在所讲的Otis Redding，他的跨界成绩是排名第41位、第35位。来到1966年，Otis Redding的代表作《Try a Little Tenderness》在流行榜单上排名第25位，在R&B榜单上则是第4位。所以，谈到Stax和Motown，如果你只是去看榜单排名，Motown确实在很多方面更胜一筹；但是话说回来，Stax在音乐和风格上其实产生了更大的影响。1967年春天，Otis Redding出席了盛大的Monterey Pop音乐节，和Booker T. & the M.G.'s一起表演。Steve Cropper说过，那是一次很奇怪的演出签约，因为当时他们带的是常见于俱乐部的小扩音器，服装则是全套的马海毛西装，诸如此类；而现场都是些嬉皮士，其使用的设备是Marshall Stack和Les Paul等等。他心想，自己这些便携扩音器还顶什么用呢？但是他们就这样完成了表演，这场表演也被视为Otis Redding的传奇时刻。它让Redding与“嬉皮士运动”关联起来，众多的嬉皮士就此将他的音乐传播出去，使之抵达了更广泛的受众群体。可惜好景不长，他在1967年12月死于空难。彼时他已经录完了自己的标志性歌曲《Sittin' On the Dock of the Bay》，到1968年初，也即他早逝后不久，这首歌同时登上了流行榜单和R&B榜单的第1位。在商业层面上，这对Stax来说是件噩耗，因为他是少数几个真正与Stax签约的艺人之一。Otis Redding的遇难，给Stax的运营工作留下了很大的缺口。我知道这种说法多少有一些不敬，但是事实大致如此。
现在来讲讲Sam & Dave。Atlantic签下了这个组合，但又把他们“租借”给了Stax。换言之，Jerry Wexler早就签下了他们，但是前者说：我要把你们送到孟菲斯、和Stax的人共事，因为我喜欢Stax所做的工作。所以Sam & Dave和Isaac Hayes、David Porter有很密切的合作关系，他们共同推出了一系列热门单曲，其中都有Stax的乐队、“Stax号声”的身影。最重要或者说最知名的一首歌也许是《Soul Man》，它在1967年登上了R&B榜单的第1名，在流行榜单上则排名第2。它也是The Blues Brothers在1979年翻唱的众多歌曲之一。1979年，John Belushi和Dan Aykroyd一同组建了The Blues Brothers；他们的首次亮相是在周六夜现场 (Saturday Night Live)上 ，之后又拍了自己的电影等等。这部电影再度激发了人们对那批歌曲的热情，Duck Dunn、Steve Cropper和Aretha Franklin等音乐人都现身其中。The Blues Brothers在1979年推出的电台版本歌曲，实际上非常接近Sam & Dave的原版。这对于Sam & Dave来说当然是件好事，他们的职业生涯焕发了第二春；之前从未得到过的高报酬的演出要约，如今突然纷至沓来。总之，这就是Sam & Dave，一个签约于Atlantic，却租借在Stax旗下的组合。
这和Wilson Pickett的情况很相似，他同样是签约于Atlantic而在Stax旗下发行唱片。他最知名的歌曲之一，《In the Midnight Hour》，在1965年夏天登上了R&B榜单首位和流行榜单的第23位。它实际上是Steve Cropper和Wilson Pickett一起创作，并由孟菲斯录音棚的乐队在当地录制的。Steve Cropper讲过这首歌曲的背后故事：Wilson Pickett在寻找灵感的时候会即兴地唱点东西，所唱的通常是福音音乐 (gospel) 的传统内容，比如“我主耶稣在午夜时分来到身边”；Cropper把Wilson Pickett唱的东西凑到一起，从而写成了这首歌。创作过程中，Jerry Wexler管理着整个项目，而Tom Dowd也经常造访，给前者描述纽约的孩子都在跳的一种舞蹈。这种舞的节拍是1、2、3、4，但在第2拍和第4拍上会稍作延迟，所以实际的节拍是1、-2、3、-4，而不是标准的均匀节拍。他们开始捕捉那种感觉，而这就成了所谓的延迟节拍 (delayed backbeat)。《In the Midnight Hour》取得巨大成功后，他们试图继续如法炮制。这种延迟节拍的感觉，常常会和Stax联系在一起。但当时发生了一些事情，具体经过不得而知，反正Stax的Jim Stewart禁止Wilson Pickett待在孟菲斯的Stax录音棚。Jerry Wexler知道阿拉巴马州的Muscle Shoals的南部有另一家录音棚，那里出品的声音很对他口味。比如Joe Tex的《Hold On To What You've Got》，其于1965年位列流行榜单的第5名、R&B榜单的第2名；这首歌是在Muscle Shoals的FAME录音棚制作的。而Jerry Wexler格外喜欢的是Percy Sledge的《When A Man Loves A Woman》，它在1966年夺得了R&B榜单和流行榜单的双冠军。但实际上，它的录制地点不是FAME录音棚，而是同地区的Quincy录音棚。无论如何，Jerry Wexler有一个联系密切的合作伙伴，名叫Rick Hall，其就在FAME录音棚工作。于是，他让Wilson Pickett搬到了Muscle Shoals。为了得到“Stax号声”的效果，他没有将实情告知Jim Stewart，而是直接付钱给Stax的管乐队、让他们开车来Muscle Shoals录制音轨，因为他实在想要那种号声。在《In the Midnight Hour》之后，Wilson Pickett的全部经典唱片都是在Muscle Shoals制作的。这让阿拉巴马州的Muscle Shoals在业内声名鹊起，成了最有嬉皮节奏感、最有嬉皮味道的流行乐录音地点之一。1966年的《Land of 1000 Dances》、《Mustang Sally》， 以及1967年的《Funky Broadway》，这些热门歌曲都同时登上过R&B榜单和流行榜单，而且都是在阿拉巴马州的Muscle Shoals录制的。

最后要讲的这位南部灵魂乐的代表，从很多方面来看，都是南部灵魂乐历史上名声最响、地位最高的。Aretha Franklin，其很晚才进入大众视野——讲到Aretha，我们要说的当然不再是1964、1965年的时候，而是60年代的末期。她比其他艺人更晚入行，但其他艺人的地位都比不上她。Aretha Franklin有着很好的福音音乐背景，她的父亲，尊敬的C.L. Franklin，是密歇根州底特律New Bethel Baptist教堂的牧师。他在底特律乃至全国范围内都是个名人，出席过许多全国性的活动。他还有自己的电台节目，名气确实很大。因此，他的女儿Aretha及其姐妹听过大量的福音音乐，见过很多重要的福音音乐歌手，曾和他们一起吃晚饭、开展社交活动。总之，在她还是个孩子的时候，Aretha就已经近距离接触了这些东西。对一个未来的职业歌手而言，如此背景是再好不过了的。在60年代的前半段，Aretha Franklin最初与Columbia公司签了约，但Columbia好像不太知道该怎样包装Aretha。他们似乎把她归为高级夜总会的歌手或者爵士歌手之类，当时她推出的唱片也没有取得多少成绩。Aretha与Columbia的合约将要期满时，Jerry Wexler注意到了她，并根据她的能力制定了很好的事业规划，于是劝说她转投Atlantic旗下。事成之后，他首先带Aretha来到Muscle Shoals的FAME录音室，让她和制作人Rick Hall以及那边的录音棚乐队一起工作，从而令她的音乐向福音色彩更浓的风格发展。最初一切进展顺利，至少他们完成的第一首歌，1967年发行的《I Never Loved a Man》，登上了R&B榜单的第9位和流行榜单的第37位。但是录音室里出了状况，人们开始相互争执，其中牵扯到酗酒的问题；制作团队不欢而散，那时Wexler却甚至还未做完唱片的B面。鉴于那里弥漫着敌意，他决定不再带Aretha Franklin回到Muscle Shoals。他在纽约的录音室里完成了唱片，所以事实上Aretha的很多南部灵魂乐作品都是在纽约录制的。有时候，Wexler会让Stax的管乐队或者其他乐手从南部坐飞机过来参与录音，但这些工作毕竟还是在纽约完成的。Aretha随后取得了很大的成功，她那些为人熟知的60年代单曲都是在这段时期里推出的。《Respect》在1967年拿下了R&B榜单和流行榜单的双冠军。Otis Redding听到Aretha版本的《Respect》时说，也许创作和最先录制这首歌的人是我，但如今拥有这首歌的人是她了。1968年的《Chain of Fools》拿下了R&B榜单的冠军和流行榜单的第2名，同年的《Think》登上R&B榜单首位和流行榜单第7位。这首歌也是Aretha在电影《The Blues Brothers》里客串时演唱的曲目。因此从很多方面来看，Aretha Franklin是南部灵魂乐的巅峰。讽刺的是她并不在Stax的旗下，那些唱片甚至不是在南部录制的；然而它们仍是南部灵魂乐风格的象征，和我下节课要讲的Motown音乐并驾齐驱。
在下节课，我们将通盘讨论Motown、Stax、英伦入侵和美国的回应。这几个词囊括了1960年代中期的乐坛所发生的事情。我们将试着弄清楚，以上几种音乐活动之间存在着怎样的影响和效应。
body.en:
Artists such as Aretha Franklin push southern soul forward and outward—even when the records are not wholly made in the South.
For Stax records—or more broadly southern soul led by Stax and Atlantic together—a stable roster drives the style. As last section said: unlike Motown’s sleek, professional sound, these Stax artists strike the public as more sincere; their voices are rougher, freer, more open. A few of them now.
Start with Otis Redding. Because Stax and Atlantic are tightly linked, we must separate who truly signs to Stax from who belongs to Atlantic. Otis is a true Stax signee. He has early-1960s hits; by 1965 he crosses over with songs like “Mr. Pitiful”—No. 10 R&B, No. 41 pop. Also “Respect,” written and first sung by Otis, later Aretha Franklin’s signature—we will come to that. His 1965 “Respect” is No. 4 R&B but only No. 35 pop. Recall Motown chart positions; Otis here is No. 41 and No. 35. In 1966 his signature “Try a Little Tenderness” is No. 25 pop / No. 4 R&B. So if you only read the charts, Motown often wins; musically and stylistically Stax may leave the larger mark. Spring 1967 Otis plays the big Monterey Pop Festival with Booker T. & the M.G.’s. Steve Cropper calls the booking strange: they bring club-size amps and full mohair suits; the hippies have Marshall stacks and Les Pauls. What use are these portable amps? They play anyway; the set becomes legendary for Otis, tying him to the hippie movement and carrying his music to a wider audience. It does not last: he dies in a plane crash in December 1967. He has already cut his signature “(Sittin’ On) The Dock of the Bay”; early 1968, soon after his death, it hits No. 1 pop and R&B. Commercially a blow to Stax—he is one of the few true Stax signees. His death leaves a large gap in Stax’s operation. The phrasing is a bit irreverent; the facts roughly hold.
Now Sam & Dave. Atlantic signs them, then “lends” them to Stax. Jerry Wexler has them under contract and says: I am sending you to Memphis to work with Stax; I like what they do. So Sam & Dave work closely with Isaac Hayes and David Porter on a run of hits with the Stax band and “Stax horns.” Best known may be “Soul Man”—No. 1 R&B / No. 2 pop in 1967. It is also among songs the Blues Brothers cover in 1979. That year John Belushi and Dan Aykroyd form the Blues Brothers—first on Saturday Night Live, then a film, and so on. The film revives interest; Duck Dunn, Steve Cropper, Aretha Franklin appear. The Blues Brothers’ 1979 radio version sits close to Sam & Dave’s original. Good for Sam & Dave—a second career spring; high-paying offers that never came before suddenly arrive. So: signed to Atlantic, farmed out to Stax.
Wilson Pickett is similar—Atlantic signed, Stax-issued. One of his best known, “In the Midnight Hour,” is No. 1 R&B / No. 23 pop in summer 1965. Steve Cropper and Pickett write it; Memphis studio players cut it locally. Cropper’s story: when Pickett seeks ideas he improvises—often gospel stock, e.g. “the Lord comes at midnight”; Cropper stitches what Pickett sings into the song. Jerry Wexler runs the project; Tom Dowd often visits and describes a dance New York kids are doing—counts 1-2-3-4 but with delayed 2 and 4: 1, -2, 3, -4, not even ticks. They catch that feel—the delayed backbeat. After “Midnight Hour” they try to bottle it again. That delayed feel often attaches to Stax. Then something happens—details unclear—and Stax’s Jim Stewart bars Pickett from the Memphis Stax studio. Wexler knows another southern room in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, whose sound he likes: Joe Tex’s “Hold On to What You’ve Got,” No. 5 pop / No. 2 R&B in 1965, cut at FAME in Muscle Shoals; Wexler especially loves Percy Sledge’s “When a Man Loves a Woman,” No. 1 R&B and pop in 1966—actually cut not at FAME but at nearby Quin Ivy’s studio. Anyway Wexler has a close partner, Rick Hall, at FAME. He moves Pickett to Muscle Shoals. Wanting “Stax horns,” he does not tell Jim Stewart the full story; he pays Stax’s horn section to drive to Muscle Shoals and cut tracks. After “Midnight Hour,” Pickett’s classic sides are made in Muscle Shoals. That puts Muscle Shoals on the map as one of the hippest-feeling pop recording spots. 1966’s “Land of 1000 Dances,” “Mustang Sally,” and 1967’s “Funky Broadway” all hit R&B and pop charts—all cut in Muscle Shoals, Alabama.

The southern-soul figure who, in many ways, stands highest is Aretha Franklin—she enters the wider view late: not 1964–65 but the late 1960s. She arrives later than others, yet none outrank her. Strong gospel background: her father, the Rev. C. L. Franklin, pastors New Bethel Baptist in Detroit; he is famous locally and nationally, on radio, at national events. Aretha and her sisters hear a great deal of gospel, meet major gospel singers at dinners and social events—close contact from childhood. Ideal training for a future professional singer. In the early 1960s she signs to Columbia; Columbia seems unsure how to package her—supper-club or jazz singer—and the records do little. As the Columbia deal ends, Jerry Wexler notices her, plans a career around her strengths, and persuades her to Atlantic. He first takes her to FAME in Muscle Shoals with Rick Hall and the house band, pushing a more gospel-colored style. First results work: 1967’s “I Never Loved a Man (the Way I Love You)” is No. 9 R&B / No. 37 pop. Then trouble in the room—arguments, drinking; the team breaks up before Wexler even finishes the B-side. With hostility in the air he will not bring Aretha back to Muscle Shoals. He finishes the album in New York, so much of her southern-soul work is actually cut in New York. Sometimes he flies Stax horns or other players up from the South, but the work is still New York. Then huge success: the 1960s singles everyone knows. “Respect” is No. 1 R&B and pop in 1967. Otis Redding, hearing her version, says he may have written and first recorded it, but now it is hers. 1968’s “Chain of Fools” is No. 1 R&B / No. 2 pop; same year’s “Think” is No. 1 R&B / No. 7 pop—also what she sings in her Blues Brothers cameo. In many ways Aretha is southern soul’s peak. The irony: she is not on Stax, and those records are not cut in the South; yet they still symbolize southern soul, running parallel to Motown, which we take up next.
Next section: Motown, Stax, the British Invasion, and America’s reply—words that cover mid-1960s music. We will try to see how these currents affect one another.
